newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kredietbank stock div to fund expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kredietbank stock div to fund expansion.

text.p: Kredietbank, one of Belgium's top four banks, said that proceeds of its optional stock dividend would be used to fund further expansion, notably in emerging markets and its brokerage unit.

"Our bank still has a lot of expansion plans. To secure future growth and a sound risk asset ratio, we offer an optional stock dividend," Kredietbank chief executive officer Marcel Cockaerts told a news conference on 1996 earnings.

KB director Remi Vermeiren said that if all shareholders took shares instead of cash, KB would raise a maximum of 5.2 billion francs. He said that four billion francs would be a more realistic figure, adding that KB's current majority shareholders had all said they would take shares rather than cash.
Vermeiren said that part of the funds might be used for the foreign expansion of KB's brokerage unit KB Securities, already the largest broker on the Brussels market in volume terms.
"KBS has gone 70 percent of the way in Brussels, it is time to gradually start looking for similar activities abroad," he said.
He said this could possibly be done in cooperation with KB-Petercam Derivatives.
Cockaerts said that KB was continuing to look for opportunities in growth areas such as eastern Europe, sourth-east Asia and Latin America.
The bank is in the process of establishing a merchant bank in Singapore and has requested a licence to open representative offices in Sao Paulo in Brazil and Buenos Aires in Argentina.
